speaker: Doctor
text: Welcome to the clinic, I am Dr. Agent. I understand you have had an episode of loss of consciousness; to help me determine the cause, can you tell me exactly what you were doing right before you passed out?

speaker: Patient
text: 53-year-old male. The patient was brought to the emergency department after an episode of loss of consciousness that occurred 1 hour ago, immediately after micturating. His wife found him unconscious on the bathroom floor. He regained consciousness after about 30 seconds without any confusion or amnesia for the event. No history of urinary incontinence during the event.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Postmicturition Syncope (a form of situational syncope). The sudden loss of consciousness immediately after urination, with rapid recovery and no confusion, is highly characteristic of this condition caused by a vagal response or venous pooling upon standing.
